questions.question: Analyse how case study and field study methods are applied in social and economic research. / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Analyse how case study and field study methods are applied in social and economic
  • research. [An] / [CO2]
  • Case study and field study methods are applied in social and economic research to gain
  • deep, contextual insights into real -life situations, behavio urs, and systems. They help
  • researchers understand complex phenomena by observing and analyzing specific case s or
  • environments directly.
  • Case studies focus on a single unit (e.g., person, community, institution) to
  • explore its dynamics in depth. They are useful for examining unique or deviant cases,
  • policy impacts, or social processes.
  • Field studies involve dir ect observation and interaction in natural settings,
  • allowing researchers to collect firsthand data on social and economic activities, cultural
  • practices, or community responses.
  • Both methods emphasize qualitative analysis , though they can incorporate
  • quantitative data, and are valuable for generating hypotheses, informing policy, and
  • understanding lived experiences.

questions.question: Describe the characteristics, strengths, and limitations of action research as a method of scientific inquiry.
questions.solution_html:
Comprehensive Evaluation Rubric (Essay / Long Problem):
• Introduction & Conceptual Foundation (2 Marks): Comprehensive overview, definitions, contextual scope, and historical/theoretical relevance.
• Detailed Structural Analysis & Derivations (5 Marks): Deep exploration covering all relevant dimensions, mathematical proofs, architectural diagrams, or comparative taxonomies.

questions.question: Why is randomness important in cluster sampling? / [CO1, CO2, CO3, CO4, CO5, CO6]
questions.solution_html:
• Why is randomness important in cluster sampling?
  • [K] / [CO1, CO2, CO3, CO4, CO5, CO6]
  • Randomness is crucial in cluster sampling to ensure unbiased representation of the
  • population. It ensures unbiased representation and improves generalizability of results.
  • • Reduces selection bias: Randomly selecting clusters prevents researchers from
  • choosing groups that may skew results.
  • • Improves generalizability: It helps ensure that findings from the sample can be
  • applied to the broader population.
  • • Maintains statistical validity: Random selection supports the use of probability
  • theory for estimating sampling errors and confidence intervals.
  • • Enhances diversity: Random clusters are more likely to capture varied
  • characteristics across the population.
